new_items.title: Rethinking Document Indexing for LLM-based Analysis
new_items.summary: Documents such as clinical records, legal contracts, and scientific papers are increasingly analyzed with large language models (LLMs). The naïve approach of prompting the model with the full text for every question is slow, expensive, prone to hallucination on long inputs, and reuses no work across questions. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems build reusable state to address this, but they store it as embedded chunks: slicing text into fragments can lose the meaning that spans them, and the resulting index is tied to one embedding model, so it must be rebuilt whenever that model changes. new_items.title: ContextLure: Exploiting Benign Conversation History for Indirect Prompt Injection
new_items.summary: As LLMs become more capable, agents can perform more complex tasks with tools and maintain longer interactions with users. These benign conversations contain evidence on task results, user concerns, and operational constraints. The risk is that attackers who can observe benign conversations (evidence) may construct stronger indirect prompt injections without increasing the attackers' control over prior turns or the later injection. However, we still lack a clear study of how effectively attackers can select and use this evidence. To address this gap, we introduce ContextLure, a red-teaming framework in which an attacker silently observes an existing benign conversation, extracts evidence, and constructs an injection.
